summary.headline: No findings detected in the audited sample.

opportunities.title: No schema.org JSON-LD exists on sampled ja.wikipedia.org articles, but this is not treated as a comparable defect to sites like eff.org's -- a real, different, and more authoritative machine-readable channel already exists and is explicitly linked from every article
opportunities.rationale: The sampled article (jawiki 'Japan') has zero JSON-LD and no meta description, which would ordinarily be evidence worth flagging. But it links explicitly to its corresponding Wikidata entity (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityPage/Q17), a structured knowledge base entry maintained independently of the page's own HTML, and Wikipedia/Wikidata are already a foundational data source most AI systems draw on directly rather than by scraping article HTML for JSON-LD. This is the same reasoning this project applied to arxiv.org's Highwire citation tags: a materially different situation from a site with no machine-readable presence anywhere, and treating them identically would be a false positive against a site that is, empirically, among the most-cited sources across AI assistants today despite lacking on-page schema.org markup.
opportunities.mechanism: Not applicable as a fix -- this entry exists to record the reasoning for *not* flagging an absence, so a reader of this report understands why the finding that would appear on a similarly-structured commercial site does not appear here.

not_assessed.reason: The sampled article's declared language (ja) is non-English; per this skill's own documented exception, the density-threshold classifiers (English-only keyword patterns) do not apply and were not run against Japanese text. A definitional opening sentence is present on direct inspection (standard for Wikipedia's lede-paragraph convention), but no systematic question-coverage derivation was performed in this run.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot state a coverage percentage; this is a scope limit of this run, not a claim about the article's actual quality, which reads as substantive on direct inspection.

not_assessed.reason: Not systematically checked in this run. Wikipedia's standard footer convention states a last-modified date in visible text, but this was not confirmed to be present as parseable markup (a <time> element or JSON-LD dateModified) on the sampled page in the time available.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot confirm whether the last-modified date is machine-extractable specifically, versus only human-readable.

not_assessed.check: Engagement and rendering-fidelity checks across a broader sample (engagement-audit, render-extractability-audit)
not_assessed.reason: This run hand-verified one article page in depth (chosen specifically to exercise non-ASCII URL handling) rather than a stratified sample across article types (disambiguation pages, list articles, stub articles).
not_assessed.impact: The one page sampled delivered full, real text with no JavaScript dependency; a broader sample was not attempted.
